thread:
claire: Observed p95 host ingress rise (~10%) after kern-tile/2026-03-19. Root looks like tokenization -> extra write syscalls.

matt: can you share a condensed profile?

claire: short perf cut: 
```
35% host::tokenize::split_norm
20% host::parse::proto_unwrap
12% net::http2::hpack_encode+flush
9% io::writev_syscall
6% kvcache::evict
```

sam: that hpack + writev combo smells like more small writes per streamed response. any kernel change to chunk alignment?

claire: yes. kernel tile size for utf path moved to 2KB which splits previously coalesced buffers. write counts per req jumped ~2x in canary metrics.

proxy-bot: deploy: kern-tile rolled to prod-stable at 2026-03-19T06:07Z (rev: kern-tile-20260319).

matt: quick mitigations: 1) toggle ingress small-write coalescer flag on canary, 2) add tokenizer write batching (host-side), 3) revert tile-size if needed.

sam: also audit batch packing alignment -> rounding could reduce effective tokens/batch causing more streams.

claire: repro cmd for local:
```
./tools/benchmark --concurrency 40 --payload ./payloads/2k-mixed.json --http2 --duration 30s
```

claire: will ship micro-metrics today: host.tokenize.write_calls, http2.hpack.flush_count, parse.kvcache_evictions sampled 1%. posting updates after coalescer test on canary.

matt: good. if coalescer brings p95 down, we'll keep kernel change and add a kernel-selection rule to preserve old alignment for streaming routes.

claire: update 3152223400: canary coalescer ON -> immediate drop in write_calls (~-48%) and p95 trending back toward baseline. continuing to monitor.
